R16.summary: The nuncio in Paris to Rome, 7 March 1586: Guise sends word through the Ferrarese ambassador that the King means to make peace with the heretics once he has the money from the sale under the bull, and that he will never consent; Guise would accept the peace for Metz and a good sum of money; the King's heart does not match his show of confidence, and Guise is about to leave; the clergy's congregation, discontent with the alienation, inclines to appeal to a future council; the nuncio offers to send their letters in his cipher.
R16.en:
7 March 1586. From France.

Today the Duke of Guise sent word to me through the ambassador of the Duke of Ferrara that he now holds it for certain
that the Most Christian King must make peace with the heretics as soon as he has collected what is to be sold under the
bull, but that the Duke of Guise will never consent to it; and that he has also written what he means to answer the
Most Christian King if he raises it with him, and he showed it to the ambassador, who added that what was written said
in substance that the Duke of Guise neither could nor would consent to that peace. That the Most Christian King really
has this in mind I gather is now believed by others too, and above all by the prelates of the congregation.
